children: The energy firm will acquire the Greater Ekofisk Area oilfields and its 40.25% interest in the Teesside terminal near Middlesbrough in the UK for an agreed enterprise value of $4.425bn.

Var said the deal would further strengthen its position as the largest independent exploration and production company in Europe, while raising its long-term production target to above 500,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day into the mid 2030s.
ConocoPhillip’s Norway business produced around 120,000 boepd in 2025.

Torger Rod, chief operating officer, added: “We are adding a highly complementary portfolio of long-life assets and a highly-experienced and competent team. The increased scale across our operated portfolio creates significant opportunities for further value creation.”

ConocoPhillips first confirmed last month it was considering a possible sale of the assets, having received an unsolicited approach, in line with an ongoing strategy to “optimise and high-grade” its portfolio.
Norway’s Ekofisk field was the oil-rich country’s first major discovery, made in 1969 by Phillips Petroleum, which was acquired in 2002 by Conoco to create the current business.

ConocoPhillips chief executive Andy O’Brien said: “Norway and Teesside are high-quality assets with strong operating histories, and we believe this win-win transaction unlocks value for ConocoPhillips while positioning these assets for continued success under new ownership.”
Completion, which is dependent on regulatory approval, is slated for the first quarter of 2027.
As at 1230 GMT, Var Energi’s Oslo-listed shares were up 3% while ConocoPhillip’s New York- listed stock was 1% higher in pre-market trading.
